source.name: BBC World News RSS
source.title: Europe targeted by spiralling campaign of sabotage - and Russia is the chief suspect
source.summary: Germany has blamed Russia for an attack on Leipzig airport but there has been a series of suspicious incidents elsewhere.
source.evidence_text:
The BBC described a rise in suspected sabotage targeting European military and defence facilities.
Germany attributed an attack involving explosive drones at Leipzig airport to Russia, whose officials rejected that accusation.
Fires had occurred at defence-related facilities in multiple European countries.
Some governments had blamed Russia, whereas other cases were still under investigation and some fires might prove accidental.
Leipzig airport was used by Ukraine to transport military supplies.
Investigators in Estonia were taking possible Russian sabotage seriously after a factory fire and two arrests.
Slovak police reported preventing a fire attack against a Ukrainian-owned drone business and arresting suspects.
One analyst interpreted the suspected campaign as pressure on countries providing support to Ukraine.
Another analyst argued that Russia was testing European vulnerabilities and the willingness of governments to respond.
The report identified Russia as the principal suspect in the wider campaign, without establishing responsibility for every incident.
source.evidence_kind: Editor-written factual notes paraphrased from the linked BBC article; not quotations or independent reporting.
